Bursar Uktar, or simply Uktar, serves the Guild as elected bursar.[1] He appears during Act Three and is located before the entrance to the bar in the Guildhall.
“
You are not known to me. For supplies, seek the bugbear. To trade trinkets, the Fetcher's Brats.
„
— Uktar, displaying his charm[2]

Involvement

Act Three

Uktar is first found inside  Nine-Fingers Keene's office, arguing with her about an orphanage which has fallen behind on its payments and how they should resolve the matter while also upholding the Guild's reputation. At a break in the conversation, Uktar notices the party's presence and reprimands them for listening in, before Nine-Fingers takes over and becomes the focus of the conversation.

Afterwards, if a party member starts a conversation with Uktar for the first time, they can make a History check on the origins of his name:

  • [HISTORY] 'Uktar'. Ponder where you know the name from. (DC 15)

Passing this check reveals that "Uktar" is the 11th month of the year, more commonly known as 'the Rotting', the time in which all things decay and die. Uktar reveals that the name was given to him by Nine-Fingers, and the party can remark that there appears to be no love between him and Nine-Fingers.

Uktar is an alternative to  Tut Thistlebog as a source for the  Stone Lord's plans. If  Jaheira is in the party when meeting with  Nine-Fingers Keene, but not the one speaking, the information is delivered automatically, which truncates the interaction with Tut.

His name also appears in the text of multiple books which discuss Guild activities in recent (game world) history.

Vault Key Business

Uktar offers a ransom for High Security Vault Keys[3] for the ⁠Counting House – but only if the contents of the corresponding vault remain untouched. For each one delivered to Uktar, he responds with a unique comment corresponding to the previous owner of the key. This comment is the same whether or not the vault itself has been looted.

  • Give him Cazador's key.
    • Uktar
      Ah. A rather ancient patron of the Counting House. He has accrued quite a bit of interest, I'd wager.
  • Give him Gortash's key.
    • Uktar
      Ah, the would-be Duke! I'm sure he parted with it on good terms.
  • Give him Glitterbeard's key.
    • Uktar
      Glitterbeard. He was given mastery of the counting house over me, you know. Well deserved, wouldn't you say?
  • Give him Grey's key.
    • Uktar
      Wonderful, thank you.
  • Give him Lady Jannath's key.
    • Uktar
      A fine and noble house. Their funds will serve the city, as they would wish.
  • Give him Lorroakan's key.
    • Uktar
      The great wizard. I will be interested to see what manner of curiosities he deems worth locking away.
  • Give him Nine-Fingers' key.
    • Uktar
      A most peculiar key to have in your possession. I wonder who it belongs to. Here is your compensation.
  • Give him Ravengard's key.
    • Uktar
      The returning hero of Elturel. He's the philanthropic sort, so I'll assume this was a gift, yes?
  • Give him Viconia's key.
    • Uktar
      DeVir. Now what would a servant of Lady Loss be so keen on keeping safe?

Under Lock and Key (gold rewards)

If the party deliver a key to Uktar which belongs to an unopened vault,[verify] they receive a gold reward[verify] along with the usual unique line of dialogue. A pop-up – similar to what happens when a quest awards an item – appears after exiting the conversation with Uktar. Even though no corresponding quest appears in the journal, the text on these pop-ups is labelled as "Under Lock and Key," and also the following text is displayed: "We sold [Character]'s vault key to Guild Bursar Uktar."

Combat

Uktar has no special combat abilities. He cowers and does not enter the initiative order if combat is started nearby.
